official-report-of-the-exploration-of-th: Newton Chittenden's state report sets down the survey of British Columbia's Queen Charlotte Islands — their shores, woods, mines, and native towns. Made for the men who would rule the isles' fate, it is packed with things seen at first hand. Now it aids students of the past as a close-up view of the islands in the late 1800s.
seventy-five-receipts-for-pastry-cakes-a: Eliza Leslie's 1828 cookbook was one of the first cookbooks published by an American woman, and it became a kitchen classic. Its seventy-five receipts — the old word for recipes — cover cakes, pastries, and sweets in the plain style of the early republic. A delicious piece of American culinary history.
the-life-of-venerable-sister-margaret-bo: This biography honors Marguerite Bourgeoys — Sister Margaret — who founded Montreal's Congrégation de Notre-Dame in the 1600s and devoted her life to teaching. Her courage in the wilderness settlement made her one of Canada's great religious figures. An inspiring life, reverently told.
the-idol-of-paris: Sarah Bernhardt, the divine Sarah herself, wrote this novel of Paris — the stage, its idols, and the fierce passions behind the footlights. Who better to tell the tale of theatrical life? A star's-eye view of the world she ruled, glittering and candid.
the-history-of-pendennis: Thackeray's beloved Pendennis follows Arthur Pendennis from wayward youth to manhood — through London literary life, love, and loss. The author's warmest, most autobiographical novel charms every reader. A masterpiece of Victorian fiction. Blanche Amory, the Major, and Warrington live as vividly as old friends.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-diss: This 1913 Catholic reference piece on Disentis — the old monks' house high in the Swiss Alps — traces its long life through war and peace. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: The Encyclopedia on Saint-Denis, the burial church of French kings. Royal tombs crowd its Gothic choir. George Cyprian Alston details its splendor. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-ecche: This 1913 reference piece on Abraham Ecchelensis — the Maronite scholar who taught in Rome. Anthony Maas notes his Arabic learning. He served popes and the Vatican press. East meets West in one learned life. His Arabic Bible aided the polyglot scholars.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acta-sanctae-: A 1913 entry on the Acta Sanctae Sedis — the Holy See's official record of decrees. Its pages carried Rome's voice to the world. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adeste-fideli: A 1913 entry on Adeste Fidelis — O Come, All Ye Faithful, the Christmas hymn of hymns. Joseph Otten traces its authorship. Wade's Latin rings each December. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aeterni-patri: This 1913 reference piece on Aeterni Patris — Leo XIII's great encyclical on St. Thomas. Michael O'Riordan explains its call. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-nat: A 1913 entry on Alexander Natalis — Noël Alexandre, the Dominican historian. Arthur McMahon honors his vast folios. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-of-: This 1913 reference piece on Alexander of Lycopolis — the Egyptian who refuted the Manichaeans. John Joseph A'Becket notes his treatise. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexis-paulin: A 1913 entry on Paulin Paris — the French scholar of medieval romance. Louis Delamarre praises his editions. His Romans de la Table Ronde charmed readers. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alton-illinoi: This 1913 reference piece on Alton, Illinois — the old diocese of the Mississippi. Francis Zabel traces its pioneer days. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amastris: This 1913 reference article on Amastris — the Paphlagonian city by the sea. Its bishops grace the old councils. Homer's Paphlagonians lived nearby. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-analysis: This 1913 reference article on analysis in logic — the resolving of wholes into parts. Charles Dubray treats the scholastic method. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anastasiopoli: A 1913 entry on Anastasiopolis — the city of the Resurrection's name, now a titular see. Its bishops grace the old lists. The Church keeps its hopeful name. A see of the eastern empire. The name outlives the city. Its walls recall Justinian's engineers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antipatris: A 1913 entry on Antipatris — the city of Paul's night journey. The entry traces its scriptural mention. Soldiers bore the apostle through its gates. Herod's city kept the coastal road. A name in the Acts. Its walls are lost to the sands.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apocatastasis: This 1913 reference piece on apocatastasis — the hope of universal restoration. Pierre Batiffol traces the old debate. Origen dreamed all might be saved. catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apodosis: A 1913 entry on the apodosis — the leavetaking of the feast. Andrew Shipman explains its Eastern use. The feast's farewell repeats its joy.
